$comment: ★★★ A FOREIGN OBJECT'S PAGE-OFFSET LOADS (P68 round 9, D-LK-MACHO-ARM64-PAGEOFF12-LOAD-PATCHED-AS-AN-ADD). A reference compiler reaches a global as `adrp` + a load whose 12-bit offset field the LINKER fills, and that field is scaled by the access size. Mach-O spells every such field with ONE relocation type, ARM64_RELOC_PAGEOFF12, and the linker takes the scale from the instruction, as ld64 does; ELF spells the scale in the type (R_AARCH64_LDST8/16/32/64/128_ABS_LO12_NC). ✔MEASURED 2026-09-23 at the round-9 base: the Mach-O arm LINKED (rc=0) and wrote the UNSCALED page offsets, so `_get` read `[x8,#0x700]`, `[x9,#0x60]`, `[x10,#0x100]`, `[x11,#0x140]`, `[x12,#0x300]` while the objects sat at page offsets 0x70, 0x30, 0x40, 0x50 and 0x60 of a 0x80-byte `__data` (llvm-objdump of the image); only the byte load was right. The ELF arm was REFUSED ('relocation type 299 ... is not declared'). aarch64 gcc 13 -O2 links the ELF archive and runs it to 42 under qemu. Both arms must now run to 42: the Mach-O one on the macOS leg, the ELF one under qemu.

prebuiltLibraries.$comment: aarch64-linux-gnu-gcc 13.3.0 `-O2 -fno-section-anchors -c` + aarch64-linux-gnu-ar `rcs`: every global gets its own `adrp` + LDSTn_ABS_LO12_NC load, all five scales. The witness is a definition's own name.

clang 18.1.3 `--target=arm64-apple-macos11 -O2 -c` + llvm-ar `rcs`: ARM64_RELOC_PAGE21 + ARM64_RELOC_PAGEOFF12 on ldr q (16), ldrsb (1), ldrsh (2), ldr w (4) and ldr d (8). The witness is the Mach-O-decorated name, which only this container spells.
